content.text: I've just set up a Shure mv7+ microphone, and I've plugged it into my MacOS laptop. I'm wondering if there are any settings I need to tweak, or if this should work by default. I've just got it plugged in via USB-C.

The MV7+ is class-compliant USB audio, so it should just work with no drivers. A few things worth checking though:

**Make it the input device**
- System Settings → Sound → Input → select "Shure MV7+". macOS often keeps the built-in mic selected after you plug something in.
- Some apps (Zoom, Teams, OBS, DAWs) have their own device picker and may ignore the system default—check there too.

**Sample rate (optional but tidy)**
- Open Audio MIDI Setup (in /Applications/Utilities). Select the MV7+ and set the format to 48 kHz. If a video app requests a different rate than the device is set to, macOS resamples, which is fine but 48 kHz is the safest default for calls/video.

**Gain and DSP — this is the part that actually matters**
- The MV7+ has onboard processing (auto level, EQ presets, compressor, limiter, popper stopper, reverb) plus a touch panel. Out of the box it's typically in **Auto Level Mode**, which handles gain for you and is fine for calls.
- To adjust anything—input gain, monitor mix, the LED colour, turning the DSP off for a cleaner signal—you need Shure's **MOTIV Mix** app (Mac App Store or shure.com). This is the only way to change most settings; macOS itself only exposes a basic input-level slider.
- If the touch panel gets nudged, it's easy to accidentally mute (the LED turns red) or change the volume. You can lock the panel in MOTIV Mix.

**Monitoring**
- Plug headphones into the mic's 3.5 mm jack for zero-latency monitoring. The monitor mix knob (in MOTIV Mix, or via the touch panel) blends your voice against computer playback.
- If you also want the MV7+ as your **output** device (so calls come through those headphones), select it under Sound → Output as well.

**Mic technique**
- It's a dynamic mic, so it wants to be close—roughly 2–10 cm from your mouth, speaking into the end (front) of the capsule, not the side. Farther away and it'll sound thin and pick up room noise.

**Also check**
- If you plan to use the XLR output at the same time, note the XLR is analogue only and bypasses the DSP.
- Make sure you're on the USB-C port directly on the laptop or a decent hub; some cheap hubs cause dropouts.

Short version: select it in Sound → Input, install MOTIV Mix to set gain/DSP and lock the touch panel, and get close to the mic.

I've also recently installed the Adam D3V nearfield speakers. These are plugged in via USB-C, and they seem to be working fine, but are there any other settings I would want to configure on the MacOS computer that's running them?

The D3V is also class-compliant USB audio, so "working fine" is the expected state. A few things worth tuning:

**Output device and volume behaviour**
- System Settings → Sound → Output → confirm "ADAM Audio D3V" is selected. Same caveat as the mic: apps like Zoom/Teams/DAWs have their own picker.
- Over USB, macOS's volume slider controls the D3V digitally. Set the speaker's physical volume knob to a fixed reference (say 12 o'clock) and use macOS for day-to-day volume, or vice versa — just don't fight both. Two volume stages means it's easy to end up with a low digital level padded by a high analogue gain, which costs you resolution and adds noise.
- If the macOS volume slider is greyed out for the D3V, the device isn't exposing a USB volume control and you'll be on the knob only. That's normal for some monitors.

**Sample rate**
- Audio MIDI Setup → select D3V → set 48 kHz (or 96 kHz if you're mainly listening to hi-res material — the D3V accepts up to 96 kHz). As with the mic, macOS resamples anything that doesn't match, so this mostly matters for keeping calls/video and music consistent. 48 kHz is the sane default if you also use the MV7+ at 48 kHz.
- Check the bit depth is 24-bit while you're there.

**Pairing with the MV7+**
- If you want speakers for output and mic for input, that's just two device selections and no extra setup.
- If you want to use them together in a DAW (Logic, Ableton, Reaper) as one device, create an **Aggregate Device** in Audio MIDI Setup with the D3V as clock source and drift correction enabled on the MV7+. Not needed for calls or general use.
- On calls, use headphones through the MV7+ rather than the speakers, or you'll get echo. macOS/Zoom echo cancellation helps but a dynamic mic at 5 cm with speakers a metre away is asking for feedback into the call.

**Speaker-side DSP**
- The D3V has rear switches for room placement (desk, wall proximity) and a bass tilt. Set these for your desk position — nearfield on a desk typically wants the "desk" compensation on and a slight low-end cut if they're against a wall. Nothing on the Mac controls this.
- No official ADAM software exists for the D3V; all speaker configuration is physical.

**Avoid**
- Don't route the D3V through a Bluetooth or AirPlay path if you can help it; wired USB direct to the laptop or a powered hub.
- Skip macOS "Sound Effects" going to the monitors (Sound → Sound Effects → play on "Selected Sound Output Device" vs the internal speakers) if you don't want alert pings blasting through them at listening level.

Short version: pick a single volume control, set 48 kHz/24-bit in Audio MIDI Setup, set the rear placement switches for your desk, and use headphones on calls.
